classification.difficultyReason: Combine return-trip calculations with different wind-adjusted speeds and a fixed total-time constraint.

content.prompt: The pilot of an ultra-light aircraft has determined that the plane averages 75 km/h in still air.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If she flies out for 20 km and then returns by the same route, how long will she take?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Total distance} &= 20+20=40\text{ km}\\\text{Total time} &= \frac{40}{75}=\frac{8}{15}\text{ h}\\\text{Total time} &= \frac{8}{15}\times60=32\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If she flies out for 1 hr 42 min and back for 1 hr 42 min, how far does she travel in total?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Time each way} &= 1+\frac{42}{60}=1.7\text{ h}\\\text{Total time} &= 2\times1.7=3.4\text{ h}\\\text{Total distance} &= 75\times3.4=255\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: If there is a 40 km/h headwind as the pilot flies out and a 40 km/h tailwind on return, what is the longest time the pilot can fly out to be able to return in 4 hours? (Answer in hours and minutes.)

inlines.text: Use equal outward and return distances with speeds of 35 km/h and 115 km/h.

answer.worked:
The outward speed is $75-40=35\text{ km/h}$ and the return speed is $75+40=115\text{ km/h}$. Let $t$ hours be the outward flying time. For the longest outward flight, the total time is 4 hours, so the return takes $(4-t)$ hours. The distances are equal.
$$\begin{align*}35t &= 115(4-t)\\35t &= 460-115t\\150t &= 460\\t &= \frac{46}{15}\text{ h}\\t &= 3\text{ h}+\frac{1}{15}\times60\text{ min}\\t &= 3\text{ h }4\text{ min}\end{align*}$$
